'''''Campanula poscharskyana''''', the '''Serbian bellflower''' or '''trailing bellflower''', is a semi-[[evergreen]] trailing [[perennial plant|perennial]], valued for its lavender-blue star-shaped flowers. It is [[native plant|native]] to the [[Dinaric Alps]] in former Yugoslavia.<ref>A-Z Encyclopedia of Garden Plants, The American Horticultural Society</ref>

==Description==
The [[leaf|leaves]] are {{cvt|2.5|-|4.0|cm|frac=4}} long. The shoots grow along the ground, reaching about {{cvt|20|-|25|cm|frac=4}} long. They then grow upwards, placing the flowers about {{cvt|10|cm}} above the ground. Flowers are lavender-blue and bloom from mid-[[spring (season)|spring]] to early [[autumn]].

==Cultivation and uses==
This tough [[rockery]] plant bears sprays of violet starry flowers in spring and summer. Vigorous and fast growing, it is able to stand drying out once established in a wall. It will self-seed into cracks in walls and paving.

During winter, it survives best at {{convert|5|-|10|C|F}}, but can tolerate both colder and warmer temperatures. Although it is considered winter hardy, many growers bring it indoors and keep it in slightly moist soil on a windowsill, or in the basement under a lamp.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

It is common to cut the plant down during the fall, so it can conserve energy during the winter, and then replant it in spring. In winter, no fertilizer is needed.

Plants can be grown from stem [[cutting (plant)|cuttings]] or [[division (horticulture)|division]] of the roots.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://growherbsgarden.com/campanula-poscharskyana/ |title= How To Grow Campanula Poscharskyana  }} Monday, 8 July 2019 </ref>

Numerous [[variety (botany)|varieties]] and [[cultivar]]s have been developed for garden use, including 'Blue Gown', 'Blue Waterfall', 'Freya', 'E.H. Frost', 'Glandore', 'Lisduggan Variety', 'Senior', and 'Silberregen'. The cultivar 'Stella' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Campanula poscharskyana'' 'Stella'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/99779/Campanula-poscharskyana-Stella/Details | accessdate=15 April 2020}}</ref> 

The leaves are edible year round, and can be put in salads.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pfaf.org/user/cmspage.aspx?pageid=39|title=Winter Salads|website=www.pfaf.org}}</ref>

==Pests==
[[Thrips]] and [[aphid]]s feed on the leaves.
